mechanism: SGLT2 inhibitors as adjunct to insulin in T1D
note: Adults with T1D on insulin: insulin-deficient rodents (STZ rat, Akita and NOD mouse) predicted the glucose lowering, but no rodent model reported the euglycaemic ketoacidosis that decided the class's fate in T1D; rats reproduced it only post hoc (2019) and only with insulinopenia plus dehydration.
label: T1D (SGLT2 adjunct)

engagement.note: Dapagliflozin cut blood glucose up to 55% in insulin-deficient STZ rats: first in-vivo evidence the renal target works without insulin.
engagement.short: Dapagliflozin lowers glucose in STZ rats
engagement.quote: The C-aryl glucoside 6 (dapagliflozin) was identified as a potent and selective hSGLT2 inhibitor which reduced blood glucose levels in a dose-dependent manner by as much as 55% in hyperglycemic streptozotocin (STZ) rats.
engagement.judgement: Abstract-level. The FDA pharmacology review for NDA 202293 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2014/202293Orig1s000PharmR.pdf) confirms the STZ rat was the filed insulin-deficient model: 'The STZ-treated rat is a model of insulin deficient diabetes ... Following a single oral dose (0.01-0.1 mg/kg) dapagliflozin produced a dose-dependent reduction in blood glucose'. Han 2008 (Diabetes) is the fuller pharmacology paper; Meng 2008 is the verified discovery paper and carries the same STZ result.

engagement.note: Empagliflozin abolished glomerular hyperfiltration in Akita T1D mice; in hyperfiltering T1D patients it cut GFR by 33 mL/min, same drug, same tubular mechanism.
engagement.short: Hyperfiltration fell 33 mL/min in T1D patients
engagement.quote: During clamped euglycemia, hyperfiltration was attenuated by -33 mL/min/1.73m(2) with empagliflozin in T1D-H, (GFR 172±23-139±25 mL/min/1.73 m(2), P<0.01).
engagement.reason: Akita hyperfiltration result held in T1D patients
engagement.judgement: Juxtaposition, not a stated comparison: Vallon 2014 (https://doi.org/10.1152/ajprenal.00520.2013, epub Nov 2013) reported empagliflozin 'completely prevented the diabetes-induced increase in glomerular filtration rate (GFR) (255 vs. 397 μl/min)' in Akita mice; Cherney 2014 (NCT01392560, 40 T1D patients, 8 weeks empagliflozin 25 mg, results posted 2014-06-17) found the same direction in patients. Only abstracts read, so whether Cherney cites Vallon's Akita data directly is unverified (hence medium). The simpler engagement read-out from the same trial, Perkins 2014 (https://doi.org/10.2337/dc13-2338): 'Mean urinary excretion of glucose increased from 19 ± 19 to 134 ± 61 g/day (P < 0.0001)', matches the glycosuria every rodent study showed. Akita mice were an academic model (Vallon, UCSD), not named in the FDA/EMA reviews, so model_filed is false; the STZ rat (2008 entry) was the filed model.

dose.note: Rats gave a dose–response (0.01–0.1 mg/kg), but T1D doses were inherited from T2D trials; no rodent-to-patient exposure comparison was ever published.
dose.quote: The C-aryl glucoside 6 (dapagliflozin) was identified as a potent and selective hSGLT2 inhibitor which reduced blood glucose levels in a dose-dependent manner by as much as 55% in hyperglycemic streptozotocin (STZ) rats.
dose.judgement: The T1D phase 3 doses (dapagliflozin 5/10 mg, DEPICT-1; empagliflozin 2.5/10/25 mg, EASE; sotagliflozin 200/400 mg, inTandem) were the T2D doses plus, for empagliflozin, a lower 2.5 mg arm added for safety. The FDA pharmacology review documents the rat dose–response ('dose-dependent reduction in blood glucose which was statistically significant at 0.03 and 0.1 mg/kg') but no model set an exposure target for T1D. The one dose-dependent clinical finding that mattered, DKA rising at 10/25 mg but not 2.5 mg (Rosenstock 2018), had no rodent counterpart. Status untested rather than an empty list because the model was used for dose–response in the filed package.

efficacy.note: Glucose fell 55% in STZ rats with no endogenous insulin: the premise that SGLT2 inhibition adds glucose lowering on top of insulin in T1D.
efficacy.quote: The C-aryl glucoside 6 (dapagliflozin) was identified as a potent and selective hSGLT2 inhibitor which reduced blood glucose levels in a dose-dependent manner by as much as 55% in hyperglycemic streptozotocin (STZ) rats.
efficacy.judgement: Later T1D-specific models carried the same prediction: Akita mice (Vallon 2014, empagliflozin lowered blood glucose from 517-535 to 187-237 mg/dl) and NOD mice on low-dose insulin (Powell 2015, https://doi.org/10.2147/DMSO.S76342: 'Sotagliflozin significantly improved glycemic control, without increasing the rate of hypoglycemia measurements, in diabetic mice maintained on a low insulin dose'). The NOD study is the only rodent experiment designed as adjunct-to-insulin T1D and is the model the EMA Zynquista assessment report (EMA/178275/2019) names in its nonclinical pharmacology section.

efficacy.note: NOD mice on low-dose insulin matched high-dose insulin's HbA1c with sotagliflozin; inTandem3 patients cut HbA1c 0.46 points and bolus insulin 2.8 U/day.
efficacy.quote: A significantly larger proportion of patients in the sotagliflozin group than in the placebo group achieved the primary end point (200 of 699 patients [28.6%] vs. 107 of 703 [15.2%], P<0.001).
efficacy.reason: Insulin-sparing glucose lowering held in patients
efficacy.judgement: Abstract-level juxtaposition of Powell 2015 (NOD mice, sotagliflozin + 0.05 U insulin) with inTandem3 (NCT02531035, n=1402). The same direction held across the class: DEPICT-1 dapagliflozin (Dandona 2017, https://doi.org/10.1016/S2213-8587(17)30308-X, NCT02268214, results posted 2018-03-29) HbA1c -0.42%/-0.45% vs placebo; EASE empagliflozin (Rosenstock 2018, https://doi.org/10.2337/dc18-1749, NCT02414958 results posted 2018-11-20, NCT02580591 posted 2018-11-02) -0.54%/-0.53% at 10/25 mg. Magnitude is direction_only: mouse HbA1c units do not scale to the ~0.4-0.5 point clinical effect. EMA's assessment report puts the NOD result in the nonclinical section, so model_filed is true. The 2019 regulatory outcomes (FDA refusal, later EU withdrawal) were on DKA, not efficacy, and do not change this cell.

safety.note: Insulin-deficient rats were read for glucose only; neither this paper nor the FDA pharmacology review for dapagliflozin mentions ketones or acidosis.
safety.quote: The C-aryl glucoside 6 (dapagliflozin) was identified as a potent and selective hSGLT2 inhibitor which reduced blood glucose levels in a dose-dependent manner by as much as 55% in hyperglycemic streptozotocin (STZ) rats.
safety.judgement: Checked by text search: the FDA pharmacology/toxicology review for NDA 202293 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2014/202293Orig1s000PharmR.pdf, 271 kB of extracted text, STZ and ZDF rat studies present) contains zero occurrences of ketone, ketosis, ketoacidosis, beta-hydroxybutyrate or acidosis. The EMA Zynquista report's nonclinical section (NOD mice) likewise has no ketone finding; every ketone mention is clinical. One rodent study did show the signal early: Devenny 2012 (https://doi.org/10.1038/oby.2012.59), dapagliflozin in diet-induced obese rats, 'Fasting BHBA was elevated in the 1 mpk, 5 mpk, and 5 mpk PF-V groups', but it was framed as a fuel shift supporting weight loss, in an insulin-replete model, and was never carried into the T1D models. Akita (Vallon 2014) and NOD (Powell 2015) papers report no ketone measurements in their abstracts.

safety.model: Insulin-deficient rodents (STZ rat, Akita and NOD mouse)
safety.note: Diabetic ketoacidosis 3.0% vs 0.6% on sotagliflozin, 5× placebo; no insulin-deficient rodent model had reported ketosis, let alone acidosis.
safety.quote: The rate of diabetic ketoacidosis was higher in the sotagliflozin group than in the placebo group (3.0% [21 patients] and 0.6% [4], respectively).
safety.judgement: Called contra on the model's silence, as in the ad-amyloid safety cell: the filed models predicted nothing about ketoacidosis and patients got it. Same signal across the class: EASE (Rosenstock 2018) adjudicated DKA 4.3%/3.3% at empagliflozin 10/25 mg vs 1.2% placebo; DEPICT-1 (Dandona 2017) adjudicated definite DKA 1%/2% vs 1% at 24 weeks; EMA pooled sotagliflozin data (EMA/178275/2019, https://www.ema.europa.eu/en/documents/assessment-report/zynquista-epar-public-assessment-report_en.pdf) 'diabetic ketoacidosis (4.0% and 5.7% vs. 1.0%)'. EMA's own mechanistic account is physiological, not model-based: 'SGLT2 inhibitors trigger multiple mechanisms that could predispose to DKA'. The only rodent reproduction is post hoc: Perry 2019 (https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-019-08466-w, comparison stated in the paper) 'Here we show that the SGLT2 inhibitor (SGLT2i) dapagliflozin promotes ketoacidosis in both healthy and type 2 diabetic rats in the setting of insulinopenia through increased plasma catecholamine and corticosterone concentrations secondary to volume depletion', citing T1D incidence of 6-20% from Garg 2017 and Peters 2016. Note Perry used 48-h-fasted normal SD rats and STZ-nicotinamide/high-fat T2D rats and explicitly excluded rats with insulin <125 pM 'indicating type 1 diabetes', so even the post hoc model is not a T1D model, and the authors caution the rodent-human weighting of dehydration vs insulinopenia may differ. Contra overrides, so 2019 does not add an entry. Later regulatory outcomes (FDA complete response letters for sotagliflozin and dapagliflozin in T1D, 2019; EMA approvals 2019 later withdrawn) are not public primary documents and were not used for the status.
